title: How Apple Makes $4,200 Profit Every Second
description:
How does Apple make so much money? In fiscal 2026 (year to Sept 26, 2026) Apple's net income was $132.2 billion: about $363 million a day, or roughly $4,203 every second. Devices like the iPhone bring in most of the sales, but Services (App Store, iCloud, Apple Music and more) are the profit engine: 26% of sales, yet 40% of gross profit, with a 76.2% gross margin versus 39.3% on products.

Sources: Apple Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 (fiscal year ended Sept 26, 2026; SEC EDGAR); Apple newsroom, "Apple reports fourth quarter results" (Nov 2, 2026). Per-day and per-second figures are our own math: net income divided by the 364-day fiscal year. Gross margin is sales minus the direct cost of those sales, before operating costs and tax; Apple says its fiscal 2026 products margin was helped by product mix and tariff refunds. Apple's App Store fees have been challenged by regulators and courts, which is a risk to Services profits. This is a business explainer, not investment advice.

scenes.say: Apple clears four thousand two hundred dollars profit every second. From what?
Fiscal twenty twenty-six profit: one hundred thirty-two billion dollars.
Most sales are devices like the iPhone. Services are about a quarter.
But here's the twist: the smaller part is the profit engine.
After direct costs, Apple keeps seventy-six cents per Services dollar. Devices: thirty-nine.
Services: a quarter of sales, but forty percent of gross profit.

The lesson: one sale pays once. A loyal customer pays again and again.
